question: The heat produced in an electric circuit is proportional to ______.
solution:
The correct answer is** (current)2** .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Joule's Law of Heating**

 
 
• The amount of heat produced in a conductor is directly proportional to:
 
• The square of the current (I²) flowing through it. 
 
• The resistance (R) of the conductor. 
 
• The time (t) for which the current flows. 
 
• This relationship is mathematically expressed as:
 
 
 
• **H = I²Rt **
 
 
• where:
 
• H is the heat produced in joules (J) 
 
• I is the current flowing through the conductor in amperes (A) 
 
• R is the resistance of the conductor in ohms (Ω) 
 
• t is the time for which the current flows in seconds (s)
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Heat Produced in an Electric Circuit
 
• When an electric current flows through a conductor, it encounters resistance.
 
• This resistance hinders the free flow of electrons, causing them to collide with the atoms of the conductor.
 
• These collisions result in the conversion of electrical energy into heat energy.
 
• This phenomenon is known as the heating effect of electric current.
